newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil called 50 cts up, Brent 5 cts higher.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil called 50 cts up, Brent 5 cts higher.

text.p: IPE oil futures were expected to open higher on Tuesday with Brent seen gaining five cents initially and gas oil anticipated putting on 50 to 75 cents, brokers said.
Good buying late on Monday brought most contracts well above their lows at the close and the upward momentum generated then was continuing, dealers said.
"The market closed reasonably well after testing lows and that has generated an encouraging response," said one broker.
IPE Brent closed down six cents at $18.93 a barrel on Monday while gas oil settled $1.75 off at $169.50 a tonne.

Monday's weakness was caused by fears the summer gasoline rally could be ending, with reports that Tosco's mammoth Bayway cat cracker might be back up after a three-week shutdown acting as a selling trigger.
But with Tosco keeping the health of the cracker swathed in mystery, rumours the largest gasoline-producing unit in the world might be back in action died down and gasoline regained strength.
"The gasoline closed one and a half cents off its lows and it had been leading the way down," said one broker. "The market performed well and was unwilling to break lower."
"We'll see a bit of upward follow through today I expect," said another broker.
Simex Brent was offered at around $19.03, confirming the positive tone, but had not traded.
Gas oil was seen as having ground to make up after closing near support levels of $169 but another quiet day's trade was expected.
